# Introduction

Genetic access to one cell type often needs a combination of marker genes:
intersectional tools such as split-GAL4 label only the cells that express
*both* genes of a pair. Single-cell RNA-seq atlases tell which genes each
cluster expresses, but choosing a combination by hand means comparing hundreds
of clusters at once, often across developmental stages, sexes or species.

**scMarco** makes that search systematic. Expression is first binarized per
cluster with a Bayesian mixture model [@davis2020], so each gene is ON, OFF or
ambiguous in each cluster and in each *split* of the data (stage, sex,
species, ...). scMarco then

* ranks the candidate markers of a cluster by their off-target clusters;
* ranks gene pairs by the clusters in which both genes are ON;
* finds genes that tell apart the off-targets of a first marker;
* plots the ON/OFF states, co-expression, expression levels, UMAPs and the
  mixture-model fit of each gene.

scMarco was first developed to select split-GAL4 lines for the fly visual
system [@Chen2023.02.03.527019].

Everything is available both from R, as shown here, and in an interactive
Shiny app (Section \@ref(the-shiny-app)).

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("scMarco")
```

# A first dataset

scMarco datasets are [AnnData](https://anndata.readthedocs.io) (h5ad) files,
read with *[rhdf5](https://bioconductor.org/packages/rhdf5)* so that single
genes can be read without loading whole matrices:

* `<id>.clusters.h5ad` (required) holds one row per split and cluster, with
  the mixture model's probability of expression of every gene and, optionally,
  the fraction of cells with UMIs (`pct_pos`) and cluster-average expression
  (`mean_lognorm`);
* `<id>.cells.h5ad` (optional) holds the log-normalized expression of every
  cell and its reductions (UMAPs).

The package ships a small synthetic dataset with both files: eight clusters
of fly optic-lobe-like neurons and glia, split by sex.

```{r load}
library(scMarco)
toy <- system.file("extdata", package = "scMarco")
ds <- ds_load("toy", list(
    label = "Toy dataset",
    clusters = file.path(toy, "toy.clusters.h5ad"),
    cells = file.path(toy, "toy.cells.h5ad")
))
ds$splits
ds$cluster_labels
length(ds$all_genes)
```

Clusters have a stable ID, used everywhere, and an optional name shown as
`name (id)`. Cluster 8 has no cells in females; scMarco keeps track of which
clusters exist in which split, so an absent cluster is never mistaken for one
that is OFF.

# Binarization

`ds_binarize()` turns the probabilities into calls with an *ambiguity band*
centered on 0.5 and `band_width` wide: a gene is ON above the band, OFF below
it, and ambiguous inside it. The app's default width is 0.6, so ON is at
P(On) >= 0.8, OFF at <= 0.2, and 0.2-0.8 is ambiguous. Ambiguous calls never count as ON,
but they do count as possible off-target expression, so a combination is never
made to look more specific than the data support.

```{r binarize}
b <- ds_binarize(ds, band_width = 0.8)
b$on["Kr", , "Male"]
```

# Finding markers

## From a cluster

`from_cluster()` lists the genes ON in a cluster, fewest off-target clusters
first. Split criteria say in which splits a gene must be ON: here, in at
least one sex.

```{r from-cluster}
from_cluster(b, ident = "1", required = character(0), min_n = 1)
```

To require expression in both sexes, list them in `required` (or raise
`min_n`):

```{r from-cluster-both}
from_cluster(b, ident = "2", required = c("Male", "Female"), min_n = 2)
```

## Gene pairs

When no single gene is specific, a pair can be. `pair_offtargets()` ranks the
pairs of candidate genes by the clusters in which *both* are ON:

```{r pairs}
pair_offtargets(b, ident = "2", required = character(0), min_n = 1, limit = 5)
```

`find_pairs()` runs the same search for every cluster of a dataset.

## From a gene

`clusters_expressing()` goes the other way: which clusters express a gene, or
all genes of a combination?

```{r from-gene}
clusters_expressing(b, "Kr", required = character(0), min_n = 1)
clusters_expressing(b, c("Kr", "pdm2"), required = character(0), min_n = 1)
```

## Telling clusters apart

A first marker usually labels a few clusters. `distinct_within()` finds genes
that mark exactly one (or `k`) of them and none of the others, so that the
pair labels a single cluster:

```{r distinct}
others <- clusters_expressing(b, "hth", required = character(0), min_n = 1)
others
distinct_within(b, others, required = character(0), min_n = 1)
```

# Plots

ON/OFF states of the candidates, one panel per cluster (gray is ambiguous):

```{r onoff, fig.height = 4}
onoff_plot(ds, b, genes = c("hth", "hb", "Optix", "acj6"),
           idents = c("1", "4", "6"))
```

Co-expression of a combination in every cluster that expresses any of its
genes, with the fraction of cells co-expressing them:

```{r coexp, fig.height = 4}
coexp_plot(ds, b, c("hth", "hb"), show_pct = TRUE)
```

Expression levels behind the calls, per cell and per sex:

```{r box}
box_plot(ds, "dsx", highlight = c("2", "5"), interactive = FALSE)
```

Cells on the UMAP, colored by a gene:

```{r umap}
umap_plot(ds, "X_umap_full", color_by = "gene", gene = "hth")
```

And the mixture-model fit behind a gene's calls, with each cluster placed on
the fitted curve:

```{r mixture, fig.height = 7}
mixture_plot(ds, "hth", model = "Male", highlight = c("1", "4", "6"),
             band_width = 0.8)
```

# Building a dataset

New datasets are built in two steps:

1. `seurat_to_h5ad()` writes both files from a Seurat object whose metadata
   holds each cell's split and cluster ID (or one object per split);
2. the mixture model of @davis2020 (adapted from its
   [opticlobe](https://github.com/fredpdavis/opticlobe) code) is fit per split
   with `fit_mixture()` and called with `call_mixture()`, or outside R with the
   [mixture_modeling_smk](https://github.com/chenyenchung/mixture_modeling_smk)
   pipeline, and `add_probability()` adds its output, one table per split.

`make_pseudobulk()` pools each cluster's raw counts into the model's
samples, as `Seurat::AggregateExpression()` does: one sample per library
(`method = "metadata"`), or random parts. `call_mixture()` binarizes a gene
when its two-state fit beats a single Gaussian at a false discovery rate of
10%, its ON and OFF levels are apart (Ashman's D of at least 2) and its
chains agree; it flags calls to treat as ambiguous: chains that disagree, ON
with too few cells detecting the gene, and OFF with more UMIs than the
ambient RNA estimated by `ambient_summary()` (DecontX) explains. Every cut is
an argument, and the values in use are printed. `qc_report()` summarizes the
result per split.

```{r build, eval = FALSE}
seurat_to_h5ad("neurons.rds", "neurons", out_dir = "data",
               split_col = "sex", cluster_col = "seurat_clusters",
               split_label = "sex")
# per split: raw counts of its cells, cluster IDs and libraries
pb <- make_pseudobulk(counts, cluster, method = "metadata", group = library)
fit <- fit_mixture(pb$lognorm, pb$cluster, pb$replicate)  # chunks: merge_mixture_fits()
amb <- ambient_summary(counts, cluster, library)
male <- call_mixture(fit, amb)
qc_report(fit, male, amb, file = "qc/neurons_Male", dataset = "neurons", split = "Male")
saveRDS(male, "male_prob.rds")
# one table per split; add external = TRUE for tables from outside scMarco
add_probability("data/neurons.clusters.h5ad",
                c(Male = "male_prob.rds", Female = "female_prob.rds"))
```

`validate_h5ad()` checks a dataset before it is deployed, and
`set_cluster_names()` and `set_cluster_metadata()` annotate clusters in
place, without rewriting the data:

```{r annotate}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".clusters.h5ad")
file.copy(file.path(toy, "toy.clusters.h5ad"), path)
set_cluster_names(path, c("3" = "T4/T5"))
get_cluster_metadata(path)
report_validation(validate_h5ad(path), path)
```

Datasets from the two earlier versions of scMarco convert with
`sqlite_to_h5ad()` and `h5v1_to_h5ad()`.

# The Shiny app

The app is configured by a YAML file that lists the datasets, optional gene
lists to restrict the searches to (e.g. transcription factors, or genes with
available driver lines) and the page's title, theme and introduction:

```yaml
title: "scMarco"
readme: [readme/intro.md]
datasets:
  toy:
    label: "Toy dataset"
    clusters: data/toy.clusters.h5ad
    cells: data/toy.cells.h5ad
    subset_by: [class]       # let users search within part of the dataset
gene_list:
  tfs: {path: gene_lists/tfs.txt, label: "Transcription factors"}
```

Relative paths are relative to `root`, by default the working directory.

```{r app, eval = FALSE}
run_scmarco("config.yaml")
```

`scmarco_app()` returns the app object instead, for an `app.R` file on a Shiny
server: `scMarco::scmarco_app("config.yaml")`.
